transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m having trouble keeping my mind on one thing. At work, at the bench, I’ll go from a customer email to a mark I need to saw, then some noise outside, and then I realize I’ve lost track of the whole work order. It’s been getting in the way.
Did you have the same kind of trouble staying focused when you were a child?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being talked about much when I was a kid… if it was there, nobody made a big thing of it.
Have there been times when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?
Yeah… there have been stretches like that. I’d sleep maybe two or three hours and still get up feeling pretty clear, like I was ready to start cutting stones or posting designs before sunrise.
During those times when you slept only a few hours, did you feel unusually powerful or more capable than other people?

Yeah… I guess so. After I won that ribbon, I felt like I’d proved something. Like I was on another level with the jewelry work, and I could take any custom order and make it into something nobody else around here could really match.
During those times when you slept only a few hours, did you find yourself taking on a lot more projects or working much more than usual?

Yeah… I did. I’d start a lot at once—lining up new commissions, messaging old customers, planning a website, sketching out this whole Appalachian-style collection. It felt like it all needed to happen right then.
During those high-energy times, did you find yourself talking much more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I noticed that as much… maybe I was a little more keyed up, but talking more? I don’t know.
During those high-energy times, did you feel unusually euphoric or irritable?
Yeah… after the show I felt really lit up, like bigger than myself, I guess. But I’d also get irritated fast if someone told me to keep normal hours or slow down.
During those high-energy times, did they ever get so severe that you had to be hospitalized?
No… I don’t think it ever got to that point. At least, I wasn’t hospitalized for it.
Did those high-energy periods usually last at least four days in a row?
Yeah… it was more than four days. The worst stretch started right after that jewelry show award, and it kind of ran on for… about two weeks, I think.
During those high-energy periods, did you do things that were unusually risky or impulsive for you?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I probably made some quick decisions, but I don’t know if I’d call them risky. Nothing I really want to get into.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah… I guess so. It’s been more like a month now, this low, guilty feeling just kind of hanging over me most days.
During this past month, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I haven’t really been paying attention to what I enjoy lately.
During this past month, have you had trouble concentrating nearly every day?
Yeah… some. At work I’ll just kind of stare at a repair ticket, or a tray of sapphires, and I can’t keep the measurements in my head long enough to figure out what I’m supposed to do next.
During this past month, have you had much less interest or pleasure in your usual activities?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I haven’t been thinking about it much… things just kind of feel flat, I guess.
During this past month, have you had a poor appetite or been eating much more than usual?
I haven’t really noticed. My eating’s been… normal, I guess. Nothing that stands out.
During this past month, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?
Yeah… I mean, I haven’t made any plan or anything. But I do keep thinking my family, or even clients, would be better off if I wasn’t around. It comes up more than I’d like, and it scares me.
During this past month, have you been feeling tired or low on energy nearly every day?
Yeah… most days. At work my arms feel heavy, like lead almost. Even just polishing a setting or carrying a tray of stones wears me out, and resting doesn’t really fix it.
Are you thinking about killing yourself right now?
Right now… not like I’m about to do it. I don’t have a plan. But the thoughts are there—like my family and clients might be better off without me—and it scares me how often it comes up.
During those high-energy periods, did you feel driven to get a lot more done than usual?

Yeah… I did. I started trying to line up new commissions, messaging old customers, making plans for a website, sketching this whole Appalachian collection… all at the same time. It felt like I had to get it moving right then.
Did this past month of feeling low start after something particularly stressful happened?
I don’t know… not one thing I can point to. It just kind of settled in, I guess.
